name: Argha Dey CTF Challenge Methodology
description: Systematic approach to CTF challenges covering cryptography, steganography, forensics, and web exploitation. Based on patterns observed in CPENT-style CTF challenges.
examHabits: steghide steghide steghide — try the same passphrase multiple times
Check metadata with exiftool on every file first
Try CyberChef for common encodings (base64, base32, URL, hex, ROT13, binary, Morse)
binwalk -e firmware/images to extract embedded files, then examine each
XOR with common keys: 0x41 (A), 0x20 (space), single-byte bruteforce
quickRef: file <target> | binwalk -e <target> | steghide extract -sf <file> -p <pass> | exiftool <file> | cyberchef decode

decisionPoints.action: file <target> — identify true file type (magic bytes can lie)
decisionPoints.fallback: Check file size: ls -la and compare against expected content

decisionPoints.action: exiftool <file> — look for hidden comments, GPS data, embedded credentials
decisionPoints.fallback: binwalk <file> — check for appended data or embedded archives

decisionPoints.action: binwalk -eM <file> — extract and recursively analyze embedded files
echo '<string>' | base64 -d — or use CyberChef 'From Base64' recipe
decisionPoints.fallback: Try base32, base85, URL-decode, hex-decode in sequence

decisionPoints.action: CyberChef 'ROT13' or try all 26 shifts with python -c one-liner
decisionPoints.fallback: Check if text reads like English at any shift

decisionPoints.condition: Hex string found (0x-prefixed or pairs of hex chars)
decisionPoints.fallback: Check if decoded hex is another encoded layer

decisionPoints.action: CyberChef 'From Morse Code' — watch for proper spacing interpretation
decisionPoints.fallback: Manual decode: 3 spaces = word boundary, 1 space = letter boundary

decisionPoints.action: steghide extract -sf <file> -p '' (try empty passphrase first — most common in CTF)
zsteg -a <file> — checks for LSB, RGB channel, and other PNG-based hiding
decisionPoints.fallback: Stegsolve — check all color plane and filter combinations visually

decisionPoints.condition: Need to find hidden data in image
decisionPoints.action: Stegsolve — step through Red/Green/Blue planes, Alpha, and filters
decisionPoints.fallback: Check PNG chunks: pngcheck -v <file> — look for tEXt, zTXt, or unusual chunks

decisionPoints.action: hash-identifier <hash> — identify hash type, then crack with hashcat -m <mode> -a 0

decisionPoints.condition: RSA challenge with known factors n, e, c
decisionPoints.action: If p, q known: compute phi, d = modinv(e, phi), then m = pow(c, d, n)
decisionPoints.fallback: If n is factored on factordb.com, use the factors to decrypt

decisionPoints.action: Single-byte XOR: python3 -c 'for i in range(256): print(bytes([b^i for b in data]))'
decisionPoints.fallback: Multi-byte XOR: try common keys or use cyberchef Xor Brute Force

decisionPoints.condition: Memory dump or disk image received
decisionPoints.action: volatility -f <image> imageinfo — identify OS profile, then run pslist, netscan, filescan
decisionPoints.fallback: Check for embedded files with binwalk or foremost

decisionPoints.action: foremost -i <image> -o <output> — or scalpel with custom config
decisionPoints.fallback: volatility — filescan, then dumpfiles for specific file recovery

decisionPoints.action: Test SQLi auth bypass: admin' OR '1'='1' -- or admin' UNION SELECT 1,'admin','x' --
decisionPoints.fallback: Try NoSQL injection: {'$ne': null} if NoSQL backend

decisionPoints.action: Test — if filtered, try
decisionPoints.fallback: Use dalfox or XSStrike for automated payload generation
